title: Fishing in Spring, the Pont de Clichy (Asnières)

image.credit: Photograph via Wikimedia Commons (Vincent van Gogh - Fishing in Spring, the Pont de Clichy (Asnières) - 1965.1169 - Art Institute of Chicago.jpg)

highlight.text: Divisionism, also called chromoluminarism, is the characteristic style in Neo-Impressionist painting defined by the separation of colors into individual dots or patches that interact optically.

work.text: Although Van Gogh was only in Paris working among these artists for about two years, their influence can be seen here in his use of small brushstrokes of pure, brilliant color that combine to create the effect of light reflecting off the various surfaces represented in the composition.

source.author: Art Institute of Chicago
source.title: Collection description: Fishing in Spring, the Pont de Clichy (Asnières)

moment.text: Van Gogh was inspired by Signac and Georges Seurat, both of whose work is on view nearby. Their technique, called divisionism, used science-based theories of color, which they applied in individual strokes to maximize luminosity.

matters.text: Vincent would start out with a large canvas mounted on his back, then divide it up in as many sections as demanded by the motifs he found. In the evening he brought it home filled, and it was like a little portable museum, wherein were culled all the emotions of the day.

source.author: Émile Bernard
source.title: Preface, Lettres de Vincent van Gogh à Émile Bernard
